facts.a: Batu is a city in the East Shewa Zone of Oromia, Ethiopia, on the western shore of Lake Dambal (also called Lake Ziway or Hora Dambal). It lies about 160 km south of Addis Ababa on the main road to Hawassa and Moyale, at 1,643 m above sea level.
Batu was formerly known as Ziway or Zway. The lake is also known as Lake Ziway, Lake Batu, Hora Dambal or Dembel.

Lake Dambal covers about 440 square kilometres. It is 31 km long and 20 km wide, with a maximum depth of about 9 m. It is fed by the Meki and Katar rivers and drains through the Bulbula river into Lake Abijatta.

facts.q: What is the climate in Batu?
facts.a: Batu has a mild climate with a mean temperature of about 19 °C. Daytime highs are 25 to 28 °C. Rainfall is about 775 mm a year, with the wettest month in July and the driest in November.

facts.q: How many people live in Batu?
facts.a: The 2007 census counted 43,660 residents. A 2017 government estimate was 70,436 and a 2022 projection was 90,522. The city will publish its confirmed current figure.

facts.q: How many kebeles does Batu have?
facts.a: In February 2023 the Oromia regional government announced that Batu and Adami Tullu would be merged and organised into 7 kebeles. Use the Find my kebele page to see the kebele list; names and boundaries are being confirmed by the city.

facts.q: Who is the mayor of Batu?
facts.a: Ahmedin Ismail was reported as Mayor of Batu City Administration in June 2025. The Mayor's Office will confirm the current leadership on the City government page.
In an emergency call 991 for police, 907 for an ambulance, and 939 for fire and rescue. These are national short codes that work from any phone.

City offices are open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 12:30 and 13:30 to 17:30, with selected services on Saturday morning. Check each office page for its own hours. These hours are a sample until confirmed.

facts.q: What languages does the portal use?
facts.a: The portal is in Afaan Oromoo, Amharic and English. Afaan Oromoo and Amharic text is currently machine translated with Google Translate and is being reviewed by city staff.
